extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; students and critics of English literature and poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical observations about composing and judging episodes within epic poetry (illustrated by commentary on Milton's Paradise Lost). Focuses on relation to main action, character-appropriateness, diction, imagery, and moral/ethical handling of subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts which Raphael gives ... have in them those Qualifications which the Criticks judge requisite to an Episode: They are nearly related to the principal Action, and have a just Connexion with the Fable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An episode should be closely connected to the main action and the poem's fable; it should not be a digression without relation to the principal story. (Example: Raphael's accounts serve the central action.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of audience within scene
rubrics_metrics.description: The Episode ... would have been improper for her hearing, and has therefore devised very just and beautiful Reasons for her Retiring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place delicate or private episodes where it is plausible for the present characters to be absent or not privy; ensure the scene's participants make the content appropriate (avoid incongruous eavesdropping or inappropriate disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and perspicuity in handling complex matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief Points in the Ptolemaick and Copernican Hypothesis are described with great Conciseness and Perspicuity, and at the same time dressed in very pleasing and poetical Images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating abstruse or technical subjects within poetry, aim for clarity and brevity while enhancing understanding with fitting poetic imagery; do not overwhelm readers with technical exposition without lucid presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural economy: reserve episodes for expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: He would not throw it into the Relation of the six days Works, but reserved it for a distinct Episode, that he might have an opportunity of expatiating upon it more at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distinct episodes to expand subjects deserving fuller treatment rather than cramming them into unrelated sections; structural choices should allow ample room for important digressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness combined with originality
rubrics_metrics.description: These and the like wonderful Incidents ... are such as none but a great Genius could have thought of, tho, upon the perusal of them, they seem to rise of themselves from the Subject of which he treats. In a word, tho they are natural, they are not obvious, which is the true Character of all fine Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for material that feels organic to the subject yet unexpected; writing should appear natural but avoid trite or obvious choices—originality that still fits the subject is prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid imagery and sound judgment in depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Impression ... is describ'd with great Strength and Judgment; as the Image of the several Beasts and Birds passing in review before him is very beautiful and lively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depictions should combine vivid, lively imagery with sober critical judgement; sensory detail should be effective and purposeful, not merely ornamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance-over-ornament in dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: This Dialogue, which is supported chiefly by the Beauty of the Thoughts, without other poetical Ornaments, is as fine a Part as any in the whole Poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the intellectual or moral quality of dialogue carry the scene rather than relying on rhetorical or decorative flourishes; thoughtfulness in speech is a key virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of character voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poet has wonderfully preserved the Character of Majesty and Condescension in the Creator, and at the same time that of Humility and Adoration in the Creature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain distinct, appropriate registers for different characters (e.g., divine majesty vs. human humility); characters' speech and actions should consistently reflect their established nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful handling of delicate/ethical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Milton took great care to avoid all Thoughts on so delicate a Subject, that might be offensive to Religion or Good-Manners. The Sentiments are chaste, but not cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating morally or religiously sensitive topics, avoid offending prevailing standards of decency while retaining emotional warmth and sincerity—balance restraint with feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreshadowing and admonition to prepare readers
rubrics_metrics.description: These Sentiments ... gave the Angel such an Insight into Humane Nature, that he seems apprehensive of the Evils which might befall the Species ... He therefore fortifies him against it by timely Admonitions; which very artfully prepare the Mind of the Reader for the Occurrences of the next Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ admonitions or foreshadowing within episodes to prepare readers for forthcoming events; such devices should be artful and integrated, enhancing narrative forewarning without heavy-handedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance passion with reason
rubrics_metrics.description: His Discourse ... shews that his Love, however violent it might appear, was still founded in Reason, and consequently not improper for Paradise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict passions in a way that retains rational grounding appropriate to the context; extreme emotions should be shown as intelligible and tempered by reason where fitting to the setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of source material with imaginative addition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poet has interwoven every thing which is delivered upon this Subject in Holy Writ with so many beautiful Imaginations of his own, that nothing can be conceived more just and natural than this whole Episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drawing on authoritative or scriptural sources, blend faithful elements from the source with original imaginative elaboration so that additions feel just and natural rather than forced.
